fact: Fintech Association of Kenya cites Safaricom reporting almost 299,000 M-PESA agents and roughly 676,000 active Lipa na M-PESA merchants in the year to March 2025.

Fintech Association of Kenya reports that in October 2024 the CBK said banks, mobile-money companies and payment providers had achieved substantial interoperability, though partly through bilateral connections.

TechCabal reports that Equity Bank's fintech arm Finserve Africa has launched the EMMA wallet, which lets users send money, buy airtime, pay bills and save, through an Android app, USSD or the Equitel SIM toolkit.
TechCabal reports that EMMA users can push funds from the wallet into Safaricom's M-PESA merchant ecosystem, transfer balances to Airtel Money and route funds to commercial bank accounts.

Safaricom and Pesapal put M-PESA tap-to-pay and QR payment on 30,000 Pesapal terminals in Kenya, paying merchants' existing M-PESA Till Numbers, and Safaricom says scan-to-pay is available at more than 60,000 merchant outlets.
The Central Bank of Kenya reports 94.4 million registered mobile money accounts and 575,400 active agents in July 2026.
Communications Authority of Kenya data cited by TechCabal puts M-PESA's mobile money share at 88.8% and Airtel Money's at 11.1% in June 2026.
Digital Banker Africa describes Kenya as having an established mobile-money ecosystem and leadership in mobile money, with a usage gap remaining.
TechCabal reports that by July 2026 Kenya had 94.35 million registered mobile-money accounts and 575,400 agents, with KES 728.7 billion passing through the network that month, citing CBK figures.
TechCabal says Kenyan commercial banks compete over how seamlessly customers can move funds between accounts and mobile wallets.
The Communications Authority of Kenya reports 54,005,800 mobile money subscriptions and 568,463 registered agents in the quarter ended 30 June 2026.
Safaricom's M-Pesa mobile money is in service in Kenya, with 35 million Kenyan customers, per the article.
Pesalink, run by the Kenya Bankers Association's IPSL, connects banks, telcos and microfinance institutions (TechCabal).

Safaricom's M-PESA processes 37 million daily person-to-person transactions worth KES 27 billion, out of 137.9 million transactions worth KES 118 billion, with Buy Goods and Paybill serving merchant payments, per TechCabal.
Transfers between M-PESA, banks and other mobile money services such as Airtel Money pass through several platforms, per TechCabal.
Hustler Fund CEO Henry Tanui said 95 per cent of an approved Hustler Fund loan is deposited into the borrower's mobile money wallet.
Africa CDC says mobile money is widely used in Kenya, including in faster processing of health insurance payments.
KBC reports that M-PESA, a digital mobile money service, now runs its Africa-wide platform on Huawei Cloud and handles over 21 billion transactions a year across seven countries.
Business Daily reports that small traders in Kenya receive payments through M-Pesa tills and paybills.
